text:
paul (product): we need a short, actionable decision set for the private deploy roadmap: packaging formats, upgrade guarantees, and the minimum launch criteria for VPC/on-prem. goal: make field askable bullets for legal and sales.
anya (eng): baseline: support deb/rpm installers + airgapped tarball. shipping both makes installs predictable for enterprise. we should decide whether we maintain two active packaging tracks or a single canonical artifact with wrapper installers.
rafa (netops): customers also want native puppet/ansible snippets and an example iptables/bgp config that matches our recommended topology. can we commit to those as "ship-ready" at GA?
tina (solutions): field feedback: customers expect clear upgrade types: patch (hotfix), minor (non-breaking), major (breaking). they want a documented deprecation window (e.g., 90 days) and an option for paid migration assistance for majors.
omar (sre): from ops: define SLA behavior during each upgrade type. proposals: patch = no scheduled window, we can hot-patch; minor = rolling upgrade within 1h maintenance window; major = planned migration with an opt-in 4h window. for all upgrades, we promise no default IP renumbering.
paul (product): good. we need measurable launch gates. draft list: 1) packaging: deb/rpm + airgap tarball published; 2) upgrade playbook + automated preflight checks; 3) network validation tests customers can run; 4) canary tooling integrated with deploy pipeline; 5) legal bullets for maintenance windows and emergency patches. agree?
anya (eng): add: automated upgrade compatibility test matrix across last 3 agent versions and the runtime. tests must be part of CI and exposed as a compatibility report in console.
nina (solutions): (jumping in) tiny note: call the compatibility report "upgrade-readiness" and surface a PASS/FAIL and optional remediation steps. customers like simple signals.
rafa (netops): preflight example — we'll expose a validation endpoint and a kubectl job that runs network checks. sample curl for customers:
```
POST https://private.redwood.example/v1/network-check
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Body: {"peers": [{"asn": 65001, "ip": "10.10.0.2"}], "prefixes": ["10.10.0.0/22"]}
```
paul (product): legal copy we should aim for in the contract: "We will coordinate and publish maintenance windows. For non-emergency patches, 72h notice will be given. Customers retain control of IPs and BGP sessions; Redwood will not perform IP renumbering as part of automatic upgrades unless customer requests it." any legal pushes?
tina (solutions): sales wants a short spec for "migration assistance" SKUs (4h onsite equivalent remote) and a checkbox in the purchase flow. include estimated costs to set expectations.
omar (sre): runbook items: pre-upgrade snapshot of KV caches, explicit cache-invalidate on rollback, and post-upgrade health-check including token validation and model-cache warmup. expected warmup time: 90s-6m depending on model size. add to public runbook.
anya (eng): implementation note: we should support a staged rollout policy: scheduler will do 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% with configurable hold times. default holds: 5m after first, 10m after second, 15m before final. allow customer to shorten or extend.
rafa (netops): question: can customers self-trigger a rollback? i think yes but only within a limited window and with a safety interlock to prevent two conflicting rollbacks. propose: customer self-rollback allowed within 15m of a stage, after which Redwood-run rollback required.
paul (product): decision: allow self-rollback within 15m of a canary stage. Redwood will document the interlock and require an idempotent rollback token.
tina (solutions): I'll draft the field-facing FAQ and the scheduling UI copy: "Preflight checks, maintenance window, rollback window (optional), migration assistance opt-in."
omar (sre): release-bot: create rollout job when we publish GA and wire canary metrics to the release dashboard.
release-bot: rollout job created: private-ga/packaging-2026-03-21. staged policy: 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100%. watch: #release-war-room.
anya (eng): owners: eng -> packaging artifacts + CI; netops -> validation tests and BGP snippets; solutions -> playbook + field templates; legal -> contract bullets; sre -> deploy tooling + metrics. deliverable timeline: ship candidate in two sprints if all owners accept.
paul (product): final ask: create one-page decision doc with bullets we can hand to legal and sales. tina, can you produce that and include the migration SKU language?
tina (solutions): yes. target: writeup + UI copy by EOD Tue.
paul (product): thanks. followups: anya (eng) - confirm packaging track (single artifact + installers vs two tracks). rafa - share example bgp/iptables snippets. omar - add the warmup timings to the runbook. closing thread.
